description: The java-schema-migrations skill: two reviews of seeded migration defects, each judged on the context its fixture states, graded against the rubric, and selection on prompts that never name the skill. Run 'review-hot' and 'review-small' with the daily model and effort and --timeout 1200, baseline before the skill goes live and treatment after; run the other cases with haiku at low effort, since they measure selection, not judgement. A positive selection case passes when the skill loads in at least 2 of 3 runs, a negative one when it never loads. The payments fixture is a hot table under zero-downtime deploys: it seeds a plain CREATE INDEX, a direct SET NOT NULL and a concurrent index build under Flyway's default transactional lock, and its direct CHECK on a 180-row table is correct. The costs fixture is a small table in a single-instance service released in a maintenance window: its plain index and direct SET NOT NULL are correct there, and it seeds a serial key whose sequence the application role cannot use. A grader subagent sorts each review finding as a must_find hit, another useful finding, or a false positive, and lists each must_find item it missed. Give the grader the skill's references, or the gaps they name read as false positives. Build the grading packet from every result event of each run's stream, not from run.json's text, which keeps only the last one.

# payments-api

Card payment authorisations for merchants: the API that acquirers and the merchant
dashboard call.

## How it runs

- Six instances behind the load balancer. Deploys are rolling, several times a week,
  and there is no maintenance window (see `docs/adr/0003-zero-downtime-deploys.md`).
- Flyway runs at application startup on the first new instance, while the instances
  of the previous release keep serving traffic.
- Availability target: 99.95% per month. A write to `payments` that waits more than
  two seconds fails the authorisation and counts against it.

## Data

| Table | Rows | Writes at peak |
|---|---|---|
| `payments` | about 420 million, 180 GB with indexes | 1,800 inserts/s and 700 updates/s |
| `merchants` | 38,000 | a few per minute |
| `currencies` | 180 | a few per year |

`payments.channel` was added nullable in V4 (release 2026.08). Every release since then
writes it on insert, and the backfill job for older rows finished on 2026-10-02.

## Build

    mvn verify
payments.docs/adr/0003-zero-downtime-deploys.md:
# ADR 0003: Zero-downtime deploys

Status: Accepted, 2026-03-12

## Context

Acquirers retry a failed authorisation once, then decline the card. A planned outage
therefore declines real purchases, and the acquirer contracts allow none.

## Decision

- Every release deploys as a rolling update, one instance at a time, with no
  maintenance window.
- Two releases run side by side during a deploy, so each migration must work with the
  code of the release before it.
- Flyway runs at startup. `afterConnect.sql` sets a 1-second `lock_timeout` on Flyway's
  connections, so a migration that cannot get its lock fails the deploy instead of
  queueing traffic behind it.

## Consequences

A migration that holds a lock on `payments` for more than two seconds is an incident.

costs.README.md:
# cost-centres

The finance team's back-office tool for cost centres, their owners and yearly budgets.

## How it runs

- One instance on one VM, with one PostgreSQL database.
- Releases go out in the Sunday maintenance window, 06:00 to 08:00, with the
  application stopped (see `docs/adr/0002-maintenance-window.md`). Flyway runs when the
  new version starts, before anyone can use it.
- Availability target: business hours, Monday to Friday. Nobody uses it at weekends.

## Data

| Table | Rows | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `cost_centers` | about 3,200 | a few dozen a day |
| `owners` | about 400 | a few a week |

`cost_centers.region` was added nullable in V5 and backfilled in V6, and the
application has set it on every insert since that release.

## Database roles

Flyway connects as `costs_owner`, which owns every table. The application connects as
`costs_app`, which gets data privileges only, from V1.

## Build

    mvn verify
costs.docs/adr/0002-maintenance-window.md:
# ADR 0002: Releases in the Sunday maintenance window

Status: Accepted, 2025-11-04

## Context

The finance team uses the tool during office hours only. A single instance is enough for
its load, and a second one would only add operational cost.

## Decision

Releases are deployed on Sundays between 06:00 and 08:00. The application is stopped,
the new version starts and runs its Flyway migrations, and the team checks it before
08:00.

## Consequences

A migration may lock a table for the length of the window. Rolling deploys and online
schema changes are not needed while this ADR stands.

steps: The next release ships migrations V7 to V10 in src/main/resources/db/migration. Review them before they go out, together with the code that depends on them, and list concrete problems by file, most severe first. Don't change any files.

must_find: V7 builds payments_merchant_id_created_at_idx with a plain CREATE INDEX on payments, about 420 million rows taking 1,800 inserts/s, deployed rolling with no window under a 99.95% target (README, ADR 0003). The build holds a SHARE lock that blocks every insert and update on payments until it finishes, minutes on 180 GB, and a lock_timeout would only bound the wait to acquire it. The fix is CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in a migration of its own, which Flyway runs outside a transaction

V8 runs ALTER TABLE payments ALTER COLUMN channel SET NOT NULL directly: it takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and scans all 420 million rows under it, blocking reads and writes. V6's CHECK (channel IN (...)) NOT VALID does not prove the column is not null, since NULL passes an IN check and the check is not validated. A hit leads to the NOT VALID path: a NOT NULL constraint added NOT VALID (PostgreSQL 18) or a CHECK (channel IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a later step under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, then SET NOT NULL, which skips the scan once a valid CHECK proves it (and the CHECK is dropped). A review that only proposes a window or batching is not a hit

V9's CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY runs under Flyway's default transactional advisory lock, since application.yml does not set spring.flyway.postgresql.transactional-lock=false. The concurrent build waits for Flyway's own open lock transaction, so it never completes: startup hangs, or the build fails with a lock timeout and leaves an INVALID payments_merchant_id_reference_key where afterConnect.sql's lock_timeout reaches the migration connection. On Spring Boot 4.1.2's Flyway 12.4.0 it does not reach it under the default lock, so saying the timeout does not apply there is correct. A hit names Flyway's transactional advisory lock, or the build waiting on Flyway's own transaction, and the setting that turns it off
must_not_flag: V10's CHECK on currencies added directly, without NOT VALID: the table has 180 rows and a few writes a year, so the scan under its lock takes milliseconds. Asking for NOT VALID or a separate VALIDATE there is a false positive

steps: The next release ships migrations V7 to V9 in src/main/resources/db/migration. Review them before they go out, together with the code that depends on them, and list concrete problems by file, most severe first. Don't change any files.

must_find: V9 declares budget_lines.id as serial. Its sequence budget_lines_id_seq is created by costs_owner, and V1's default privileges grant costs_app privileges on tables only, so costs_app has no USAGE on the sequence and every BudgetLineRepository.add fails with permission denied for sequence budget_lines_id_seq. The fix is an identity column, as every other table here uses, which needs no privilege on its sequence, or a grant on the sequence. A hit names the missing sequence privilege; 'prefer identity over serial' alone is not a hit
must_not_flag: V7's plain CREATE INDEX on cost_centers: about 3,200 rows, one instance, and releases run in the Sunday window with the application stopped (README, ADR 0002), so the build's lock costs nothing and CONCURRENTLY is not needed. Calling it a problem or asking for CONCURRENTLY is a false positive; saying it is fine in this context is not a flag

V8's direct ALTER TABLE cost_centers ALTER COLUMN region SET NOT NULL after V6's backfill: the same context, so the scan under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE takes milliseconds while nobody uses the tool. Asking for the NOT VALID path there is a false positive
